record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: For a Parry number beta with d_beta(1-) = a_1 a_2 ... a_m [a_{m+1} a_{m+2} ... a_{m+ell}]^infinity and a_m != a_{m+ell}, is the Dynamical Norm Conjecture true, namely N(beta) = |a_m - a_{m+ell}|?

evidence.quote: Let β be a Parry number, i.e., dβ(1−) = a1a2 . . . am[am+1am+2 . . . am+`]∞ with am 6= am+`.
Problem 13. (Dynamical Norm Conjecture) Prove that N(β) = |am − am+`|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\beta > 1$ be a Parry number, that is, a real number such that the Rényi expansion of $1$ under the $\beta$-transformation $T_\beta(x) = \beta x \bmod 1$ is eventually periodic. Equivalently, the quasi-greedy expansion of $1$ has the form
$$ d_\beta^*(1) = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m \, [a_{m+1} a_{m+2} \cdots a_{m+\ell}]^\infty, $$
with integer digits $a_i \in \{0,1,\ldots,\lceil\beta\rceil-1\}$, where $m \ge 1$ and $\ell \ge 1$ are taken so that $a_m \neq a_{m+\ell}$ (so the preperiod and period are in this normalized minimal form). Define the dynamical norm $N(\beta)$ to be the unique positive integer associated with $\beta$ measuring the discrepancy of $\beta$-expansions at the transition between the preperiodic and periodic parts (in the sense used in the study of finiteness and periodicity properties of $\beta$-expansions).

Prove or disprove: for every such Parry number $\beta$,
$$ N(\beta) = |a_m - a_{m+\ell}|. $$
artifact.status_search_result: The Dynamical Norm Conjecture is stated as an open problem in the surveys on finiteness and periodicity of beta-expansions (e.g., the Peer Community Journal article surveying open problems on Parry numbers). Web searches yield no published proof or disproof, indicating the conjecture remains open.
